PCA projection and outer products

Scale the RGB values to [0, 1] and flatten the image into a column vector x with 49,152 entries. Let μ be the fitted mean and let the columns of Pk be the first k orthonormal PCA directions.

z=PkT(x−μ),z∈Rk
x^=μ+Pkz=μ+∑j=1kzjvj

The same reconstruction can be written as a sum of outer-product projections. Each vjvjT is a rank-one projection matrix.

x^−μ=(∑j=1kvjvjT)(x−μ)
About the representations

PCA represents an image using a weighted combination of shared component images. The autoencoder maps an image through a neural-network encoder and reconstructs it with a neural-network decoder.

Every original has 128 × 128 × 3 = 49,152 channel values. TAESD has a 16 × 16 × 4 latent array, containing 1,024 values. The matched-budget control changes PCA's coefficient count and TAESD's stored precision together, so their per-image byte payloads stay equal.

In the precision comparison, both representations contain 1,024 values and use the same selected 2-, 4-, or 32-bit precision. Integer modes use uniform quantization with a separate calibrated range for each coordinate. Their values are packed into actual byte payloads before reconstruction. Integer quantization uses 8,192 bytes of shared float32 range information per encoded method.

RMSE measures pixel error. Compare the pictures as well: the same error can accompany different changes in recognizable features. Reported errors use decoded values before the final rounding used to display PNG images.
